about.title: About Nona
about.description: Discover the ideas behind Longlivity by Nona: food to enjoy, everyday curiosity, and a gentler approach to wellness.
about.body:
Longlivity by Nona is a place for nourishing food, curiosity about healthy aging, and small habits that fit real life.

A thoughtful approach to living well

The journal brings together practical food ideas, quick recipes, and reflections on everyday wellbeing. Enjoyment and flexibility belong at the table, alongside an interest in nutrition.

The stories are currently editorial drafts for Nona’s review. Follow @longlivity.bynona on Instagram for the connected account.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: How this static blog works, which external services it uses, and what happens when you follow its links.
privacy.body:
Visiting this blog

This is a static website hosted on GitHub Pages. No analytics, advertising trackers, account registration, newsletter subscription, or contact forms are configured in the site code. GitHub processes technical request information when serving the site; see its privacy statement below.

Your language preference

If your browser allows local storage, choosing DE or EN saves only the language code in localStorage under longlivity.language. It stays in your browser and is not sent to us. Clear the site’s browser data to remove it. Language-specific URLs work without local storage.

External images and fonts

Photos are loaded from Unsplash and fonts from Google Fonts. Requests to these services transmit technical information such as your IP address to their providers. Visiting Instagram through a link opens an external website; there is no embedded Instagram feed.

Provider information

  • GitHub privacy statement
  • Unsplash privacy policy
  • Google privacy policy
  • Instagram privacy policy

Scope of this information

This page describes the current technical setup. The site operator’s verified identity, contact details, and any additional legally required information have not been provided. This is not a complete, legally reviewed privacy notice.

stories.title: A colorful chickpea bowl in 15 minutes
stories.description: A quick bowl with chickpeas, fresh vegetables, and a lemon dressing, using grains you have already cooked.
stories.body:
A satisfying bowl does not need a long recipe. This version combines chickpeas, crisp vegetables, and cooked grains with a simple lemon dressing. Use it as a starting point and adapt it to what you enjoy.

The photo is illustrative and does not show this exact recipe.

ingredients: 250 g cooked brown rice or quinoa (ready to eat; not dry)
240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Wash the cucumber, tomatoes, and parsley. Dice the cucumber, halve the tomatoes, and chop the parsley.
Warm the cooked grains and chickpeas in a pan over medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring, until steaming hot throughout. Add a splash of water if needed.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Divide the warm grains and chickpeas between two bowls.
Add the vegetables and parsley, drizzle with dressing, and serve.
recipe.tip: For a gluten-free version, use rice or quinoa and check packaged ingredients. Swap parsley for fresh dill if you prefer. Follow the storage and reheating instructions on pre-cooked grains.

stories.title: Make room for a walk, without making it a project
stories.description: Finding a comfortable rhythm of movement in the day you already have.
stories.alt: Sunlight falling through trees along a forest path
stories.body:
A walk can be a chance to step away from a screen, notice your surroundings, or spend time with someone you care about. There is no need to turn every outing into a performance.

Start where you are

Choose an accessible route and a duration that feels comfortable for your abilities. A short outing is a reasonable place to begin. Indoor movement and mobility adaptations can be equally valid ways to make space for activity.

If you have a health condition or are changing your activity routine, seek advice tailored to you from a qualified professional.

stories.title: A thoughtful pantry for meals that feel effortless
stories.description: Everyday ingredients that make cooking a little more inviting.
stories.alt: Olives and olive oil with fresh herbs
stories.body:
A useful pantry reflects the food you actually like to cook. Start with a few versatile ingredients rather than a long list of things you feel you should own.

A simple starting point

  • Beans or lentils, canned or dried.
  • A grain you enjoy and know how to prepare.
  • Olive oil, vinegar, and a few favorite seasonings.
  • Nuts or seeds, where suitable for your dietary needs.
  • Frozen vegetables for days when fresh ingredients run low.

Check labels for allergens and storage instructions. Choose what fits your budget, culture, and personal needs.

stories.title: A quieter beginning to your morning
stories.description: Small pockets of calm, before the rest of the day comes calling.
stories.alt: A warm cup of coffee on a table
stories.body:
Not every morning has room for an elaborate ritual. Sometimes a small pause is enough: opening a curtain, sitting with a warm drink, or taking a moment before looking at your phone.

Choose one small thing

Pick something that feels supportive rather than demanding. You might prepare breakfast the evening before, leave a book by your chair, or step outside to notice the weather.

Let your routine change with your circumstances. A useful ritual should serve your life.

stories.title: Let the season find its way to your table
stories.description: A curious, uncomplicated approach to choosing your next meal.
stories.alt: An assortment of colorful fresh produce
stories.body:
Seasonal cooking can begin with one ingredient that catches your eye. Choose something you enjoy, then build a familiar meal around it.

Keep it flexible

Roast vegetables with olive oil and herbs, fold greens into a grain dish, or serve fruit with yogurt if that suits your diet. Frozen and canned produce can also be practical choices.

There is no single perfect shopping basket. Availability, cost, taste, and convenience all have a place at the table.

stories.title: The simple pleasure of a shared table
stories.description: Making space for connection, one ordinary meal at a time.
stories.alt: A thoughtfully prepared meal at a dining table
stories.body:
A shared meal does not require a special occasion. Soup, leftovers, or a simple plate can be an invitation to pause together.

Make it easy to say yes

Keep the food uncomplicated, ask about dietary needs, and let people contribute if they would like. Connection can happen over a short lunch as easily as a long dinner.

When meeting in person is difficult, a phone call while you cook or a recipe exchanged with a friend can offer another way to stay connected.

stories.title: Protein pancakes with yogurt and raspberries
stories.description: Small pancakes made with cottage cheese and almond flour, topped with Greek yogurt and fresh raspberries: a warm breakfast in about 15 minutes.
stories.alt: AI-generated illustration of three golden pancakes with yogurt and raspberries on a light plate
stories.body:
When you feel like a warm breakfast, give these small pancakes a try. Cottage cheese and almond flour form the base, with vanilla adding a gentle aroma. Plain Greek yogurt and fresh raspberries bring a cool, tangy finish.

Keep the pancakes small to make turning them easier. Medium-low heat gives them time to cook through while the outside turns golden brown.

Trial recipe; not kitchen-tested. The image is AI-generated and illustrates a serving idea.

ingredients: 10 g protein powder with no added sugar
For the topping: 30 g plain Greek yogurt
For the topping: 15 g fresh raspberries
steps: Stir the cottage cheese and egg together in a bowl. Add the almond flour, protein powder, baking powder, vanilla and salt, and mix evenly. Small cottage cheese curds can remain visible.
Melt the butter in a nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat.
Spoon the batter into three or four small pancakes and gently flatten. Cook for about 3–4 minutes, until the undersides are golden and the edges start to set.
Turn carefully and cook for another 2–3 minutes. The centres should be cooked through; lower the heat and cook a little longer if needed.
Wash and drain the raspberries. Serve the pancakes with the yogurt and berries.
recipe.tip: Crush some of the raspberries into the yogurt to spread their juice through the topping. Contains milk, egg and almonds. Also check the protein powder label for allergens. Times are approximate; cooking takes longer if the pancakes do not all fit in the pan at once.
